summary: Use value, surface response and silhouette to study form with a deliberately restricted hue range.
objective: Neighboring parts remain distinct without hue changes, and shadows do not erase the contour under inspection.
intent_signals: Use value and light to distinguish shape
example_prompts: Make a monochrome gear study where teeth, hubs and shafts remain easy to distinguish.

principles: Use value, surface response and silhouette to study form with a deliberately restricted hue range.
This is an authored creative proposal, not a historical definition, fixed template or required rendering library.
implementation: Prioritize curvature, edge treatment and spacing because color categories will not separate adjacent parts.
Choose a value range and broad light-dark relationships; use small finish differences only when they help read the shape.
Set a stable study view and a slow orbit; hold motion when comparing geometry variants under the same light.
observable_checks: Neighboring parts remain distinct without hue changes, and shadows do not erase the contour under inspection.
Inspect the selected view and an alternate view at the intended output size before accepting the treatment.

known_limits: Proposed art direction only; no rendered artifact, runtime improvement or perceptual validation has been observed for this record.
Appearance choices do not certify factual geometry, material measurements or simulated behavior.
creative_affordances: Combine with faceted, clay or minimalist forms; retain a separate readable legend when the underlying data needs categorical distinction.
